POSTERS.title: New System. Same Warm Welcome.
POSTERS.short: On go-live day, let your smile lead.
POSTERS.intro: Our upgrade should improve the customer experience. Make every customer feel welcome, valued and supported.
steps: Bring the same warmth, patience and care to every interaction. Keep customers informed and reassured.
If a customer complains, listen calmly. If you are unsure, pause and check before answering.
Consult the relevant internal team for the information you need to serve the customer well.
Find the relevant guidebook or procedure. The information is at your fingertips — use it.
POSTERS.key: Smile. Check. Serve. Never let a system change become a reason to turn a customer away.

POSTERS.title: Keep the Welcome. Start the Process.
POSTERS.intro: During the static data freeze in the week before go-live and the first three days after go-live (Monday 1 to Wednesday 3 February 2027), account opening is unavailable in Flexcube 11.1 and Corbit X.
steps: Start in Newgen. Collect all required documents.
Receive deposits through the designated GL. Record and monitor every deposit.
Finalise from Thursday 4 February 2027 and provide account numbers.
POSTERS.say: We are upgrading our systems to serve you better. We can start your application now. Your account number will be provided from Thursday after the upgrade.
POSTERS.key: Never turn away an account-opening request because of the upgrade.

POSTERS.title: Old Number? We Can Help!
POSTERS.short: Help customers find their new account number.
POSTERS.intro: Old account numbers will continue to be accepted for more than six months after go-live. The new account number has 13 digits, and a customer's CIF gains “00” in front.
steps: Look up the new account number in Corbit X using the process covered in training.
Serve the customer and support their transaction.
Share the new account number at every interaction. Encourage its use next time.
POSTERS.note: Guidance on printing new account numbers will follow.
POSTERS.key: Look it up. Share it. Keep banking moving.

POSTERS.title: New Chapter. New Chequebook.
POSTERS.intro: Accept cheques bearing old account numbers for six months (182 days) after go-live, until 2 August 2027, subject to the usual checks. After that date, these cheques will no longer be accepted.
steps: Accept old-number cheques until 2 August 2027, subject to the usual checks.
Encourage customers to request new chequebooks early.
Explain the transition clearly and help customers with their request.

POSTERS.title: Older Chequebook? Find a Way Forward.
POSTERS.intro: Affected chequebooks recorded in the system more than five years ago will not be migrated to Corbit X and can no longer be used. These customers have been notified.
steps: Help the customer access funds through an approved alternative.
Assist with a new chequebook where required.
POSTERS.key: Do not turn the customer away. Help them find a solution.

POSTERS.title: Sunday Checks. Monday Confidence.
POSTERS.intro: On Sunday 31 January 2027, the day before go-live, BOSs will open the branch day. All branch staff will participate in live transaction and channel checks.
steps: Test deposits, branch transactions, ATMs, the mobile app and other instructed channels.
These are REAL transactions with REAL funds. Follow controls and report issues promptly.
Do not close the branch day or run end of day on Sunday.
Continue the same branch day into Monday 1 February. Run end of day at the close of business on Monday.

FAQS: When does Corbit X go live?
Corbit X goes live on Monday 1 February 2027, in every branch and department at the same time. The final cut-off on the current system is Friday 29 January at 2:00pm.
p6
Will customers' old account numbers still work after go-live?

Yes. Old account numbers will continue to be accepted for more than six months after go-live. The new account number has 13 digits, and the CIF gains “00” in front. Look up the new number in Corbit X using the process covered in training, serve the customer, and share the new number so they use it next time.
p3
Can customers still use cheques that show their old account number?

Yes, for six months (182 days) after go-live, until 2 August 2027, subject to the usual checks. After that date these cheques will no longer be accepted, so encourage customers to request new chequebooks early.
p4
What about chequebooks recorded more than five years ago?

These chequebooks will not be migrated to Corbit X and can no longer be used. Affected customers have been notified. Explain the position with care, help them access funds through an approved alternative, and assist with a new chequebook where required.
p5
Can we open new accounts during the upgrade?

Account opening is unavailable in Flexcube 11.1 and Corbit X during the static data freeze (the week before go-live) and for the first three days after go-live (Monday 1 to Wednesday 3 February). Start the application in Newgen, receive deposits through the designated GL, and finalise from Thursday 4 February. Never turn a customer away.
p2
What happens on the Sunday before go-live?

On Sunday 31 January 2027, BOSs will open the branch day and all branch staff take part in live transaction and channel checks: deposits, branch transactions, ATMs, the mobile app and other instructed channels. These are real transactions with real funds. Do not close the branch day or run end of day on Sunday; continue into Monday and run end of day at close of business.
p6
What should I do if I'm not sure how to answer a customer?
Pause and check before answering. Consult the relevant internal team, or find the guidebook or procedure in the repository. Never let a system change become a reason to turn a customer away.
p1
Will new account numbers be printed for customers?
Guidance on printing new account numbers will follow. Until then, look up and share the new number at every interaction.
p3
How do I read the new account number?

It has 13 digits. Digits 1 and 2 are the currency (00 cedi, 01 dollar, 02 pound, 03 euro). Digit 3 is the customer type (1 individual, 2 non-individual, 3 banks and others). Digits 4 to 11 are a serial number, and digits 12 and 13 are check digits. Always add “00” in front of an existing CIF.
p3
What should I do if I'm stuck?
Check the repository guide or FAQ, then ask your champion or team lead. If you are still stuck, log a Command Centre ticket with a screenshot, and update the customer while you wait.
p1
What if someone asks a customer for their OTP?
The bank never asks for a PIN, password or OTP, and you must never share your login. Tell the customer, and report anything suspicious to Fraud and Risk.
p1
